jei.immersive_tanning.info.rack: Use the rack to lean in. Lay a raw hide over the beam and draw a Tanner's Knife through the flesh where you see it: along the grain it comes away in one pass. The hide stays clean on the beam until you pick it up. Later lace a wet tanned hide into the frame, move the tension lever to Supple, Harness or Hardened, work that finish's short treatment and seat the lever: it dries by itself. Sneak-use repeats your last finish in one go.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.vat: Pour in a bucket of water, scatter bark into it and lower scraped hides (shift for the whole stack); in any order. Each hide spends tannin by size once and tans on its own clock, even while you are away. Each hide at the rim says exactly what it waits for. The paddle on the rim may stir the batch once, bringing each steeping hide a little closer. Lift tanned hides out at the hook; hoppers can supply and empty it.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.bench: Use the bench to lean in and open its pattern book. Preparing a pattern lays your leather (one finish and trait, best Integrity first) and its other components on the mat. Trace each cut line with a Tanner's Knife, seat the freed panels on the jig, press the Awl through each hole pair and draw the thread away from the seam until it closes, then tie it off. The piece waits on the output pad. Workmanship scales armor and the finish's effects.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.knife: Use on a log to strip its bark. At the rack it scrapes flesh from a raw hide; at the bench it cuts the pattern's lines. Wears once per hide or piece.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.awl: Stitches at the Leatherworker's Bench (it wears once per piece) and mends worn pieces there with Leather Scraps. In the field, keep using it to patch your most worn leather piece with a Leather Scrap.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.bark: Stripped from logs with a Tanner's Knife. One bark is one tannin charge in a Tanner's Vat.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.scraps: Offcuts from the bench. Right-click scraps onto damaged leather in your inventory to patch it; an Awl must be in your inventory. Harness leather patches best.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.hide: Dropped by animals. Hides come in three sizes; a large hide yields three leather. Hides from some creatures keep an innate trait into the finished leather. Skins and pelts from other mods (a skinned carcass, a kangaroo hide) mount on the Tanner's Rack as raw hides too.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.leather_suppl: Supple - Light & Quiet. Each piece adds movement speed and shrinks the range at which mobs notice you; supple boots keep your footsteps from sculk.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.leather_harne: Harness - Rugged & Repairable. Much more durability, and field repairs restore twice as much.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.leather_harde: Hardened - Protective. Each piece adds armor and some toughness: the best protection leather gives, still lighter than iron.

jei.immersive_tanning.info.binding: Binding Leather replaces vanilla leather: every recipe, loot table and trade that used leather uses it instead. Cut it from any finished leather. Any vanilla leather you still hold converts one to one in a crafting grid. It cuts into three Leather Scraps.

tooltip.immersive_tanning.record_only: Its finish and quality record how it was made; they change nothing about how it works
jei.immersive_tanning.record_only_note: Finish and quality are recorded on the piece; they don't change how it works.
jei.immersive_tanning.info.genetic_anima: Genetic Animals is detected automatically: its cows, mooshrooms, moobloom, llamas, sheep, pigs and rabbits drop raw hides for the usual rack, vat, finish and bench. By default the skin an animal really drops becomes the hides: its genes, coat, age and how it died decide, so a sheep or llama in wool, a burning animal or a pig may give none, and a cow's leather makes up as many hides as it is worth, sometimes a smaller one. Servers can switch to species hides instead (every adult gives its size of hide, pigs included). Anything the animal carried drops unchanged.

Binding Leather is the leather of ordinary recipes and trades, Genetic Animals' leather trades included. It is not a raw hide and never goes back on the rack: hides come only from the animals themselves.

Made at the Leatherworker's Bench from finished leather. It is still Genetic Animals' own collar or bridle: it takes the finish's colour, can be dyed and named as usual, and works on the animal exactly as before. Its finish and quality are a record of its making and give the animal nothing extra. It keeps them when you put it on or take it off.
